questions.q: What does Carlson want you to remember about your life?
a: It is not an emergency
It is a race against others
It is a test you must pass
It is a series of deadlines
questions.why: Lesson 1 says we rush around as if driving an ambulance, when life is actually not an emergency.

questions.q: What unusual exercise does the summary suggest for slowing down?
a: Make yourself bored on purpose
Write down every task you finish
Wake up an hour earlier each day
Spend a day without speaking
questions.why: Lesson 1 recommends forcing yourself to do nothing for an hour or two to rediscover peace.

questions.q: When does the summary say you should give other people a break?
a: Especially when they seem to least deserve it
Only after they apologise for their behaviour
Whenever it costs you nothing
When they have helped you before
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues that people need kindness most when they are difficult, which makes both of you happier.

questions.q: How should you decide when to relax, according to the summary?
a: Take a break whenever you actually need one
Wait for the weekend or a holiday
Save it up for a long annual vacation
Only relax once your work is finished
questions.why: Lesson 3 says relaxation should not be postponed to weekends and can happen even on busy days.

questions.q: What thought experiment does the summary offer for dealing with frustrating people?
a: Imagine what their day might be like
Picture how you would respond to them
Recall a time you were equally slow
Consider whether they are paid enough
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests putting yourself in the postal clerk's shoes to see life through their eyes.
